topics.title: Our Duties and Obligations to Government - Duties of Pupils in a School and Duties of Children in a Family (Primary 5)
topics.content:
CIVIC EDUCATION
RELIGION AND NATIONAL VALUES
THIRD TERM
WEEK 2
PRIMARY 5
THEME - OUR DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS TO GOVERNMENT
PREVIOUS LESSON - Useful and Quick Links for Second Term Plan Lesson Notes All Subjects Primary 4, Primary 5 and Primary 6
TOPIC: DUTIES OF PUPILS IN A SCHOOL AND OBLIGATIONS OF CHILDREN IN A FAMILY
LEARNING AREA
1. Meaning of duties and obligation
2. Duties of pupils in a school
3. Duties of children in a family
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to:
1. Explain common duties.
2. Mention the obligation of the pupils to family and school.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. The national anthem to identify keywords.
2. The pledge
3. The coat of arm
4. The flag
5. Federal and State motto
6. Photographs of Nigerian sports men and women.
7. Photos and citations of those conferred with national honor.
METHOD OF TEACHING - Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book
All Relevant Material
Online Information
Relevant link - Third Term Scheme of Work and Plan Lesson Note for Civic Education Primary 4, Primary 5 and Primary 6 Links
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON ONE - INTRODUCTION
MEANING OF DUTIES
Duty is a moral or legal obligation - a responsibility.
MEANING OF OBLIGATIONS
Obligation is an act expected of an individual and to which he is morally or legally bound. It is a responsibility.
DUTIES OF PUPILS IN A SCHOOL
1. Obey the school authority.
2. Obey your teachers and the class monitor.
3. Do all school work and home work.
4. Participate in all classroom activities.
5. Work hard to ensure high grades.
6. Protect the image of the school.
DUTIES OF CHILDREN IN A FAMILY
1. Be obedience to your family.
2. Run errands for their parents and older members of the family.
3. Protect their younger siblings.
4. Do house work.
5. Protect and uphold the good name and image of the family.
6. Respect your elder and care for your young ones.
7. Be hard work at home.
8. Support all members of your family.
9. Help victims of disasters.
10. Imitate the good example of your family.
11. Seek advice from your members of family.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Guides pupils to state their duties in the family, school and their community;
Pupil’s Activities - Read national anthem to identify key words.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson - duties and obligations of citizens to government.
- Next Lesson -
LESSON EVALUATION
Pupils to:
1. Explain duties or obligations.
2. State two (2) of their duties at home or school.

topics.title: Prevention of Drug Abuse and Life Coping Skills: How to Prevent Drug Abuse, Health Promotion Behaviour, Non-Governmental Organizations, Moral Responsibility and Consequences | Primary 5 (Basic 5) Third Term Week 8 Social Studies
topics.content:
PREVENTION OF DRUG ABUSE AND LIFE COPING SKILLS: HOW TO PREVENT DRUG ABUSE, HEALTH PROMOTION BEHAVIOUR, NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS, MORAL RESPONSIBILITY AND CONSEQUENCES
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 5 - THIRD TERM - WEEK 8
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - Drug Abuse: Concept of Drug Abuse, Factors Contributing to Drug Abuse, Effects of Abuse of Stimulants and Sources of Drugs | Primary 5 (Basic 5) Third Term Week 6 Social Studies
TOPIC - PREVENTION OF DRUG ABUSE AND LIFE COPING SKILLS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Drug Abuse Prevention
3. How to Prevent Drug Abuse
4. Meaning, Importance and Consequences of Life Coping Skills
5. Health Promotion Behaviour and NGOs
6. Moral Responsibility
7. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
8. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of drug abuse prevention.
2. Mention at least five ways of preventing drug abuse.
3. Explain the meaning of life coping skills.
4. Mention at least five life coping skills that can help children make good decisions.
5. Explain the meaning of health promotion behaviour.
6. Explain the meaning and roles of Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) in preventing drug abuse.
7. Explain moral responsibility and mention some consequences of drug abuse.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about drug abuse, factors contributing to drug abuse, effects of abusing stimulants, and sources of drugs.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils how to prevent drug abuse, develop life coping skills, practise healthy behaviours, understand the role of NGOs, demonstrate moral responsibility, and understand the consequences of drug abuse.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
Charts and posters on drug abuse prevention
Pictures showing healthy and unhealthy behaviours
Flashcards
Pictures of NGOs and community awareness programmes
Drug-abuse prevention posters
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Drug abuse can harm a person’s health, behaviour, education, relationships, and future. Children can protect themselves by making good choices, avoiding bad peer pressure, controlling their emotions, and asking trusted adults for help.
Healthy habits such as eating good food, exercising, keeping the body clean, getting enough rest, and avoiding harmful substances help children stay healthy. Parents, teachers, health workers, communities, and NGOs can also help children learn about the dangers of drug abuse.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about how to prevent drug abuse, life coping skills, healthy behaviours, the role of NGOs, moral responsibility, and the consequences of drug abuse.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF DRUG ABUSE PREVENTION
Drug abuse prevention means taking steps to stop people from using drugs wrongly or harmfully.
Children can prevent drug abuse by learning about the dangers of drugs, avoiding bad company, refusing unsafe offers, and seeking help from trusted adults.
HOW TO PREVENT DRUG ABUSE
Some ways of preventing drug abuse include:
1. Avoid bad company - Stay away from people who encourage drug abuse.
2. Resist peer pressure - Learn to say “No” when someone encourages unsafe drug use.
3. Follow proper medical advice - Take medicines only as directed by qualified health professionals.
4. Learn about drug abuse - Knowing the dangers helps people make safe decisions.
5. Talk to trusted adults - Share problems and concerns with parents, teachers, guardians, or other responsible adults.
6. Avoid unknown substances - Do not accept medicines or substances from strangers.
7. Participate in healthy activities - Sports, reading, hobbies, and other useful activities can help children avoid harmful behaviours.
8. Report unsafe activities - Tell a trusted adult when someone is encouraging children to misuse drugs.
LESSON 2 - LIFE COPING SKILLS
Life coping skills are the skills people use to deal with problems, pressure, difficult situations, and challenges in healthy and responsible ways.
Examples include:
1. Making good decisions
2. Solving problems peacefully
3. Managing emotions
4. Communicating effectively
5. Resisting peer pressure
6. Asking for help
7. Thinking before acting
8. Managing time properly
IMPORTANCE OF LIFE COPING SKILLS
Good coping skills help children to:
1. Make responsible choices.
2. Handle pressure.
3. Avoid risky behaviours.
4. Deal with problems peacefully.
5. Build good relationships.
6. Develop confidence.
7. Avoid drug abuse and other harmful behaviours.
LESSON 3 - HEALTH PROMOTION BEHAVIOUR
Health promotion behaviour refers to actions that help people maintain and improve their health.
Examples include:
1. Eating balanced meals
2. Exercising regularly
3. Drinking clean water.
4. Getting enough sleep
5. Maintaining personal hygiene
6. Keeping the environment clean
7. Avoiding harmful substances
8. Seeking medical care when necessary
These behaviours help children stay healthy and reduce the risk of diseases and harmful habits.
NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS (NGOs)
Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) are independent organizations that work to help people and communities. They are not part of government.
Some NGOs help to prevent drug abuse by:
1. Educating people about the dangers of drug abuse.
2. Organising awareness programmes.
3. Supporting children and families.
4. Promoting healthy lifestyles.
5. Providing counselling and guidance.
6. Working with communities to reduce harmful behaviours.
LESSON 4 - MORAL RESPONSIBILITY
Moral responsibility means being responsible for one’s actions and choosing what is right and safe.
Children demonstrate moral responsibility when they:
1. Obey reasonable rules.
2. Make good choices.
3. Avoid harmful substances.
4. Refuse to encourage others to abuse drugs.
5. Tell the truth.
6. Respect parents, teachers, and other people.
7. Report dangerous or harmful activities.
8. Accept responsibility for their actions.
CONSEQUENCES OF DRUG ABUSE
Drug abuse can have serious consequences, including:
1. Poor health - It can damage the body.
2. Poor academic performance - Drug abuse can affect concentration and learning.
3. Bad behaviour - It may affect a person’s judgement and actions.
4. Broken relationships - It can cause problems with family and friends.
5. Dependence or addiction - A person may find it difficult to stop using a drug.
6. Financial problems - Money may be wasted on harmful substances.
7. Accidents and injuries - Drug misuse can affect judgement and coordination.
8. Legal problems - The misuse or possession of some controlled substances can have legal consequences.
ON A FINAL NOTE
- Preventing drug abuse requires good decision-making, healthy behaviours, moral responsibility, and strong life coping skills.
- Children should avoid negative peer pressure, participate in healthy activities, seek help from trusted adults, and never misuse medicines or other substances.
- NGOs, families, schools, health professionals, and communities can also help promote healthy and drug-free lifestyles.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. One way to prevent drug abuse is to ______.
A. follow bad friends
B. accept drugs from strangers
C. avoid negative peer pressure
D. visit dangerous places
2. Life coping skills help children to ______.
A. make good decisions
B. abuse drugs
C. fight with others
D. ignore their problems
3. Which of the following is a health promotion behaviour?
A. Eating nutritious food
B. Taking harmful substances
C. Avoiding exercise
D. Sharing medicines
4. NGO means ______.
A. National Government Office
B. Non-Governmental Organization
C. New Government Organization
D. National General Organization
5. Moral responsibility means ______.
A. doing whatever we want
B. refusing to obey rules
C. blaming others for our actions
D. choosing what is right and taking responsibility for our actions
B. Fill in the Gaps
Options - NGOs, exercise, responsibility, pressure, healthy
6. Regular ______ helps to keep the body fit.
7. Children should resist negative peer ______.
8. ______ can help educate people about the dangers of drug abuse.
9. Moral ______ means being responsible for one’s actions.
10. Eating nutritious food is a ______ behaviour.
C. True or False
11. Children should avoid negative peer pressure. ______
12. Life coping skills can help children handle problems in healthy ways. ______
13. Regular exercise is a harmful health behaviour. ______
14. NGOs can help create awareness about drug abuse. ______
15. Drug abuse can affect a person’s education and relationships. ______
D. Matching
16. Moral responsibility - A. Choosing what is right
17. Life coping skills - B. Helps people deal with problems
18. NGO - C. Steps taken to stop drug abuse
19. Health promotion behaviour - D. Actions that promote good health
20. Drug abuse prevention - E. Organization that helps people and communities
ANSWER KEY
1. C 2. A 3. A 4. B 5. D
6. exercise
7. pressure
8. NGOs
9. responsibility
10. healthy
11. True
12. True
13. False
14. True
15. True
16. A - Choosing what is right
17. B - Helps people deal with problems
18. E - Organization that helps people and communities
19. D - Actions that promote good health
20. C - Steps taken to stop drug abuse
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that drug abuse prevention means avoiding the wrong use of drugs.
They learned that drug abuse can be prevented by:
- Avoiding bad friends.
- Saying no to negative peer pressure.
- Making good choices.
- Taking medicines properly.
- Asking trusted adults for help.
Pupils also learned that life coping skills help us deal with problems. Examples include making good decisions, solving problems, controlling emotions, and asking for help.
They learned that health promotion behaviours include eating good food, exercising, keeping clean, getting enough sleep, and avoiding harmful substances.
Pupils learned that NGOs are organizations that help people and communities. They can educate people about the dangers of drug abuse.
Moral responsibility means doing what is right and taking responsibility for our actions. Drug abuse can cause poor health, poor school performance, bad behaviour, broken relationships, and addiction.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher shows pupils pictures of children playing, exercising, studying, and staying away from harmful substances and asks:
- What are the children doing?
- Which of these activities are good for our health?
- Why should children avoid harmful drugs?
- Who can help children when they have problems?
The teacher explains that children can protect themselves from drug abuse by making good choices, avoiding bad friends, and asking trusted adults for help.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils observe the pictures and mention healthy activities they do.
Step 2: Meaning of Drug Abuse Prevention
The teacher explains that drug abuse prevention means taking steps to stop the wrong or harmful use of drugs.
Children can prevent drug abuse by:
- Avoiding bad friends.
- Saying no to drugs.
- Following medicine instructions.
- Avoiding unknown substances.
- Asking trusted adults for help.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways they can avoid drug abuse.
Step 3: Life Coping Skills
The teacher explains that life coping skills are skills that help us deal with problems and difficult situations.
Examples include:
- Making good decisions.
- Solving problems peacefully.
- Controlling emotions.
- Resisting peer pressure.
- Communicating well.
- Asking for help.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils give examples of problems children may face and discuss safe ways of handling them.
Step 4: Health Promotion Behaviour
The teacher explains that health promotion behaviour means actions that help us stay healthy.
Examples include:
- Eating good and nutritious food.
- Exercising regularly.
- Keeping the body clean.
- Drinking clean water.
- Getting enough sleep.
- Keeping the environment clean.
- Avoiding harmful substances.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention healthy behaviours they practise at home and school.
Step 5: Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)
The teacher explains that NGOs are organizations that help people and communities.
NGOs can help prevent drug abuse by:
- Teaching people about the dangers of drugs.
- Organising awareness programmes.
- Giving advice and support.
- Promoting healthy living.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss ways organizations can help children stay safe from drug abuse.
Step 6: Moral Responsibility
The teacher explains that moral responsibility means doing what is right and accepting responsibility for our actions.
A morally responsible child:
- Tells the truth.
- Obeys reasonable rules.
- Makes good choices.
- Avoids harmful drugs.
- Does not encourage others to abuse drugs.
- Reports dangerous activities to trusted adults.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention good actions that show moral responsibility.
Step 7: Consequences of Drug Abuse
The teacher explains that drug abuse can cause:
- Poor health.
- Poor performance in school.
- Bad behaviour.
- Problems with family and friends.
- Addiction or dependence.
- Accidents and injuries.
- Legal problems.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention some problems that can result from drug abuse.
Step 8: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups.
- Group 1: Mention five ways to prevent drug abuse.
- Group 2: Mention five life coping skills.
- Group 3: Mention five healthy behaviours.
- Group 4: Mention five consequences of drug abuse.
Each group presents its answers to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 9: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the main points of the lesson, focusing on drug abuse prevention, life coping skills, health promotion behaviour, NGOs, moral responsibility, and the consequences of drug abuse.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise what they have learned.
Step 10: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils a different set of 20 questions as oral questions, a quiz, take-home work, or a quick test to assess their understanding.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Pollution: Meaning of Pollution, Sources and Causes of Air Pollution | Primary 5 (Basic 5) Third Term Week 9 Social Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. What is drug abuse prevention?
2. Mention three ways to prevent drug abuse.
3. What are life coping skills?
4. Mention three life coping skills.
5. Mention three healthy behaviours.
6. What does NGO mean?
7. Mention two ways NGOs can help prevent drug abuse.
8. What is moral responsibility?
9. Mention three consequences of drug abuse.
